title: The specified integral purity family, inverse orientation and counit trace under reduction
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\ge1$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $r\ge0$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Use the actual operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum] and twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Integral categories mean modules over the completed coefficient sheaf, derived complete with constructible reductions in one finite cohomological interval independent of $n$; finite categories mean $D^b_{ctf}(-,A_n)$. Write $H_\Lambda(L)=Lf^*L(r)[2r]$, $G_\Lambda(L)=Rf^!L$, $P_\Lambda=Rf_!$, and $\epsilon_\Lambda:P_\Lambda G_\Lambda\to\mathrm{id}$ for the actual exceptional counit. At finite levels use the specified smooth purity map [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] and trace [def-pur-smooth-trace].

Take the integral map $\gamma_{R,L}:H_RL\to G_RL$ to be the component of the simultaneous normalized natural family of [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality], with the finite reductions of [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction]. For every $L\in D^b_c(Y,R)$ this component is defined and is an isomorphism. More precisely, if $L_1$ has cohomology in $[a,b]$, all $L_n$ have Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, so $L$ belongs to the uniform finite-Tor domain of that family [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Put $\eta_{R,L}=\gamma_{R,L}^{-1}$ and $t_{R,L}=\epsilon_{R,L}\circ P_R(\gamma_{R,L}):P_RH_RL\to L$. These use this specified component throughout; no uniqueness of lifts from their finite components is asserted.

For $Q_T=(-)\otimes^L_{R_T}(A_n)_T$ let $a_L:Q_XH_RL\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{A_n}Q_YL$, $b_L:Q_XG_RL\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{A_n}Q_YL$, and $c_N:Q_YP_RN\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{A_n}Q_XN$ be the canonical pullback/twist, exceptional-adjoint and support comparisons. With $\gamma_n=\gamma_{f,L_n}$, $\eta_n=\gamma_n^{-1}$ and $t_n=\epsilon_{A_n,L_n}\circ P_{A_n}(\gamma_n)$, there are equalities of actual morphisms
$$b_L Q_X(\gamma_{R,L})=\gamma_n a_L,\qquad a_L Q_X(\eta_{R,L})=\eta_n b_L,$$
$$Q_Y(t_{R,L})=t_n\,P_{A_n}(a_L)\,c_{H_RL}.$$
The comparisons and equations are compatible with further finite quotients $A_n\to A_m$ for $1\le m\le n$, including the coefficient counits. Thus this chosen coherent integral purity realization determines an inverse orientation and a counit trace with exactly the specified finite reductions.

proof.text: Apply integral_residue_tor to the constructible input. purAdicResidueInvertible supplies the coefficient unit at every point, and the equality of predicates supplies hTor. Its interval assertion is the first conjunct of the result.

Preserve the existing quotientProjection proof, which compares the consecutive coefficient quotient sequence with the direct quotient tower and applies the inverse limit cone equation. Apply integralPurityComparisonCocycles with that projection equality to obtain all three quotient equations in the exact reductionComposition and supportComparison coordinates.

Evaluate A.finiteReductions at the finite-Tor input. It gives source and target isomorphisms and exactly the forward square for component. Reconstruction supplies finite-Tor source and target membership. Apply PurCompactSupport.reductionComparison_isIso to each; the bridges and finite realization are isomorphisms, hence so are both supportComparison maps.

Use isIso_smoothPurityMap to form e from the actual finite arrow. Cancel e.hom in the inverse square, substitute the forward square, combine the mapped component inverse and hom, and cancel their composite identity. This proves the inverse equation with this very component and e.

Apply integralPurityCounitReduction for the actual transported counit. Prove supportComparison_naturality by composing the reduction bridge, compact-support comparison, finite realization and inverse source bridge as a natural transformation. Map the definition trace=P(component) followed by counit, substitute its reduction equation, use that naturality to move component past supportComparison, and substitute the forward purity square. Functoriality gives the finite coefficient-valued smooth trace.

At every further quotient form e and e_prime from isIso_smoothPurityMap. finiteReductionOfPurity gives their forward square; cancellation as above gives the inverse square. finiteReductionOfSmoothTrace gives the trace equation, and existsUnique_finiteReductionExceptionalComparison.choose_spec.1 gives the actual counit equation. These prove FiniteEquations, including equal levels.
